revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Flooring
revealWordProblem.text: A designer is tiling an L-shaped lobby floor. The floor decomposes into a 12 ft by 8 ft rectangle and a 6 ft by 5 ft rectangle. If floor tiles cost $2.89 per square foot, what budget do you recommend the designer have for the tiles?
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Decompose the L-shape: 12 × 8 = 96 sq ft and 6 × 5 = 30 sq ft. The pieces are joined, so add: 96 + 30 = 126 sq ft. Tiles cost $2.89 per sq ft, so 126 × $2.89 = $364.14. I recommend a budget of about $365 for the tiles.

conceptIntro.heading: Let's build it together — How do we find the area of a composite figure?
conceptIntro.intro: A composite figure is a shape made of two or more simple shapes joined together. We decompose it into basic shapes, find each area, then add or subtract. We'll walk through a worked example, try one together, then you'll try a few with hints right there when you need them.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: Break the figure into simple shapes. ADD the areas when shapes are joined; SUBTRACT when a piece is cut out.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: My L-shaped room splits into two rectangles: one is 12 ft by 8 ft, the other is 6 ft by 5 ft.
First rectangle: A = length × width = 12 × 8 = 96 square feet.
The pieces are joined, so I add: 96 + 30 = 126.
So the total area is 126 square feet.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Now an L-shape made of a 5 ft by 4 ft rectangle and a 3 ft by 2 ft rectangle.
Are they joined or cut out? Joined, so we add: 20 + 6 = 26 square feet.
Sentence frame — say it with me: "The multiples/steps I need are ___ , and the answer is ___ ."

approaching.stem: An L-shaped room is made of two rectangles: 10 ft × 6 ft and 4 ft × 3 ft. What is the total area?
approaching.explanation: Area 1 = 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft. Area 2 = 4 × 3 = 12 sq ft. Total = 60 + 12 = 72 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: Double one side: area doubles.
Double both sides: area × 4.
hints: The L-shape is already split into two rectangles for you: 10 × 6 and 4 × 3.
Find each rectangle's area separately with A = l × w, then combine — joined shapes mean adding.
Compute 10 × 6 and 4 × 3, then add the two results. Label your answer in sq ft.
approaching.stemEs: Una habitación en forma de L está formada por dos rectángulos: 10 ft × 6 ft y 4 ft × 3 ft. ¿Cuál es el área total?
approaching.explanationEs: Área 1 = 10 × 6 = 60 sq ft. Área 2 = 4 × 3 = 12 sq ft. Total = 60 + 12 = 72 sq ft.

approaching.stem: A rectangular patio is 15 ft × 10 ft with a 5 ft × 4 ft rectangular flower bed cut out. What is the remaining area?
approaching.explanation: Patio = 15 × 10 = 150 sq ft. Cutout = 5 × 4 = 20 sq ft. Remaining = 150 − 20 = 130 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: Test: same perimeter, different areas?
A thin rectangle and a square can differ.
Perimeter does not determine area.
hints: The flower bed is CUT OUT of the patio — that phrase tells you which operation to use.
Find the full patio area (15 × 10) and the cutout area (5 × 4), then remove the cutout.
Compute 15 × 10 and 5 × 4, then subtract the flower bed's area from the patio's area.
approaching.stemEs: Un patio rectangular mide 15 ft × 10 ft y tiene recortado un jardín rectangular de 5 ft × 4 ft. ¿Cuál es el área restante?
approaching.explanationEs: Patio = 15 × 10 = 150 sq ft. Recorte = 5 × 4 = 20 sq ft. Área restante = 150 − 20 = 130 sq ft.

approaching.stem: Find the area of an L-shape made of a 5×3 rectangle and a 2×4 rectangle.
choiceFeedback: Area and perimeter are not linked.
A thin shape can have big perimeter, small area.
You must use both to describe a shape.
hints: Two rectangles make this L: one is 5 × 3 and the other is 2 × 4.
Joined pieces mean you add their areas after computing each one with length × width.
Find 5 × 3, then 2 × 4, and add the two products together.
approaching.stemEs: Halla el área de una figura en forma de L formada por un rectángulo de 5×3 y uno de 2×4.

approaching.stem: When should you subtract areas instead of adding them to find the area of a composite figure?
choices: When a piece is cut out or removed from a larger shape
When one shape is larger than the other
approaching.explanation: Subtract when a piece is removed from a larger shape (like a window cut from a wall). Add when two shapes are joined together (like an L-shape).
choiceFeedback: Overlap is different — subtracting is for a piece removed.
Size alone doesn't decide — subtract only when part is removed.
Not always — you add pieces that are joined together.
hints: Think of real examples: a window in a wall versus two rooms joined into an L-shape.
Ask for each choice: is material missing from the shape, or are pieces being combined?
Picture a wall with a window: you can't paint the glass, so its area comes OFF the wall's area. Match that idea to a choice.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Cuándo debes restar áreas en lugar de sumarlas para hallar el área de una figura compuesta?
approaching.explanationEs: Resta cuando se quita una pieza de una figura más grande (como una ventana recortada en una pared). Suma cuando dos figuras se unen (como una figura en forma de L).

approaching.title: Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Identify the shapes
workedExample.work: An L-shaped room is made of two joined rectangles: 8 ft × 5 ft and 4 ft × 3 ft.

workedExample.label: Find each area
workedExample.work: First rectangle = 8 × 5 = 40 sq ft. Second rectangle = 4 × 3 = 12 sq ft.

approaching.correctWork: The two rectangles are joined, so add their areas — do not multiply them. Total = 40 + 12 = 52 sq ft.
hints: Look at the last step. When two pieces are joined, do you add or multiply their areas?
Joined pieces are added: 40 + 12 = 52 sq ft, not 40 × 12.

approaching.stem: A 7 ft by 5 ft rectangle has a triangle (base 7 ft, height 4 ft) on top. Add the two areas. What is the total area?
approaching.explanation: Rectangle = 7 x 5 = 35 sq ft. Triangle = 1/2 x 7 x 4 = 14 sq ft. The pieces are joined, so add: 35 + 14 = 49 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: Scale one dimension: area scales by that factor.
Scale both: area scales by the product.
Try: if both double, area goes × 4.
approaching.stemEs: Un rectángulo de 7 ft por 5 ft tiene un triángulo (base 7 ft, altura 4 ft) encima. Suma las dos áreas. ¿Cuál es el área total?
approaching.explanationEs: Rectángulo = 7 x 5 = 35 sq ft. Triángulo = 1/2 x 7 x 4 = 14 sq ft. Las piezas están unidas, así que suma: 35 + 14 = 49 sq ft.
hints: A composite figure is built from basic shapes, so measure each shape before you think about the total.
The rectangle uses length × width and the triangle uses ½ × base × height. The pieces are joined, so their areas combine.
Rectangle: 7 × 5 = 35 sq ft. Now find the triangle with ½ × 7 × 4 and combine the two areas.
hintsEs: Una figura compuesta está formada por formas básicas, así que mide cada forma antes de pensar en el total.
El rectángulo usa largo × ancho y el triángulo usa ½ × base × altura. Las piezas están unidas, así que sus áreas se combinan.
Rectángulo: 7 × 5 = 35 sq ft. Ahora halla el triángulo con ½ × 7 × 4 y combina las dos áreas.

onLevel.stem: Plan 2 — L-shaped lobby: decompose the L into two rectangles, one 9 ft by 6 ft and one 7 ft by 3 ft, then ADD. What is the total floor area?
onLevel.explanation: First rectangle = 9 x 6 = 54 sq ft. Second rectangle = 7 x 3 = 21 sq ft. Joined L-shape, so add: 54 + 21 = 75 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: Can two shapes with same perimeter have different areas?
Yes—test with examples.
Perimeter and area are independent.
onLevel.stemEs: Plan 2 — Vestíbulo en forma de L: descompón la L en dos rectángulos, uno de 9 ft por 6 ft y otro de 7 ft por 3 ft, y luego SUMA. ¿Cuál es el área total del piso?
onLevel.explanationEs: Primer rectángulo = 9 x 6 = 54 sq ft. Segundo rectángulo = 7 x 3 = 21 sq ft. Es una L unida, así que suma: 54 + 21 = 75 sq ft.
hints: Decomposing means cutting the L into shapes you already know how to measure.
Find each rectangle's area with length × width, and note that the two pieces sit beside each other instead of overlapping.
First rectangle: 9 × 6 = 54 sq ft. Now find the second rectangle's area and combine it with the first.
hintsEs: Descomponer significa cortar la L en formas que ya sabes medir.
Halla el área de cada rectángulo con largo × ancho, y observa que las dos piezas están una al lado de la otra, sin traslaparse.
Primer rectángulo: 9 × 6 = 54 sq ft. Ahora halla el área del segundo rectángulo y combínala con la primera.

onLevel.stem: Plan 4 — Design studio: the floor is a 16 ft by 12 ft rectangle, but a 5 ft by 4 ft storage closet is cut out of one corner. Find the usable floor area.
onLevel.explanation: Large rectangle = 16 x 12 = 192 sq ft. Cutout closet = 5 x 4 = 20 sq ft. A piece is removed, so subtract: 192 - 20 = 172 sq ft.
choiceFeedback: That's the full floor — subtract the closet that's cut out.
You added the closet — it's removed, so subtract its area.
20 is just the closet — subtract it from the whole floor.
onLevel.stemEs: Plan 4 — Estudio de diseño: el piso es un rectángulo de 16 ft por 12 ft, pero se recorta un clóset de almacenamiento de 5 ft por 4 ft en una esquina. Halla el área útil del piso.
onLevel.explanationEs: Rectángulo grande = 16 x 12 = 192 sq ft. Clóset recortado = 5 x 4 = 20 sq ft. Se quita una pieza, así que resta: 192 - 20 = 172 sq ft.
hints: The closet is removed from the floor, so that corner is not usable space.
Find the area of the whole rectangle first, then the area of the cutout, and decide which operation takes one away from the other.
Whole floor: 16 × 12 = 192 sq ft. The closet covers 5 × 4 sq ft — take that piece away to finish.
hintsEs: El clóset se quita del piso, así que esa esquina no es espacio útil.
Halla primero el área del rectángulo completo, luego el área del recorte, y decide qué operación quita una de la otra.
Piso completo: 16 × 12 = 192 sq ft. El clóset cubre 5 × 4 sq ft: quita esa pieza para terminar.

onLevel.title: Level 2 Extension — Catch the Architect's Area Mistake

workedExample.label: Identify the shapes
workedExample.work: A clubhouse wall is a 18 ft by 11 ft rectangle with a triangular gable (base 18 ft, height 6 ft) joined on top.

workedExample.label: Add the areas for the total

onLevel.correctWork: The architect used the rectangle's area twice (198 + 198). Each region's area is counted only once. Total = 198 + 54 = 252 sq ft.
hints: Look at Step 4. How many regions are in this figure, and how many areas should you add?
There are only two pieces: one rectangle (198) and one triangle (54). Adding 198 twice double-counts the rectangle.

onLevel.title: Find the Area Error

workedExample.label: Identify the shapes
workedExample.work: Rectangle: 16 ft × 10 ft, with a 4 ft × 6 ft piece cut from the corner

onLevel.correctWork: Since the piece is cut out, subtract: 160 − 24 = 136 sq ft. When a piece is removed, subtract its area from the larger shape.
hints: Look at Step 4. Was the smaller rectangle added on or cut away?
The problem says the piece was 'cut from the corner,' so you should subtract, not add.

onLevel.prompt: A T-shaped room can be decomposed in two different ways. Show both ways and prove they give the same total area. Use a T-shape where the top is 14 ft × 4 ft and the stem is 6 ft × 10 ft.
onLevel.sentenceFrame: Way 1: I split it into ___ and ___. Areas: ___ + ___ = ___. Way 2: I used a ___ rectangle and subtracted ___. Areas: ___ − ___ = ___. Both give ___ sq ft.
onLevel.hint: Write original area formula and scaled formula; compare.
hints: The T's top slab is 14 × 4 and its stem is 6 × 10. Way 1 simply adds those two rectangles.
For Way 2, wrap the whole T in one big rectangle and subtract the empty corner rectangles.
Way 1: 14 × 4 plus 6 × 10. Then build the big rectangle for Way 2 and show the subtraction lands on the same total.

onLevel.instructions: Sort each composite figure by whether you ADD or SUBTRACT the areas to find the total.

items.text: Wall with a window cut out

onLevel.hint: Calculate each area and identify which is larger.
hints: Look for action words on each card: 'joined' versus 'cut out' or 'removed'.
Pieces joined together → add their areas. A hole or missing piece → subtract it from the bigger shape.
First card: the L-shaped hallway is two rectangles JOINED — pick its operation, then scan each card for its keyword.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Area of Composite Figures is adding every piece even when a piece has been cut out of the figure. For a 10 ft by 8 ft rectangle with a 3 ft by 2 ft rectangular notch cut from one corner, students compute the full rectangle 10 × 8 = 80 sq ft and stop, or they add the notch instead of removing it (80 + 6 = 86 sq ft) instead of subtracting it: 80 − (3 × 2) = 80 − 6 = 74 sq ft. Before submitting, check whether each piece is part of the figure (add it) or missing from the figure (subtract it).

questions.stem: How many triangles can you make from the center of a regular pentagon?
questions.explanation: A regular pentagon has 5 sides, so drawing lines from the center to each vertex creates 5 equal triangles.

questions.stem: A regular hexagon is split into 6 triangles, each with base 4 cm and height 3.5 cm. What is the total area?
questions.explanation: Each triangle: ½ × 4 × 3.5 = 7 sq cm. Total: 6 × 7 = 42 sq cm.

questions.stem: Using the triangle from the previous question, what is the total area of the hexagonal skylight?
questions.explanation: Total area = 6 triangles × 15.6 sq ft = 93.6 square feet.

questions.stem: A regular hexagon is divided into 6 equal triangles from the center. Each triangle has a base of 6 ft and a height of 5.2 ft. What is the area of one triangle?
questions.explanation: A = ½ × b × h = ½ × 6 × 5.2 = 15.6 square feet.
